title: Senate begins plenary debates on budget bill
summary: The Senate now girds for marathon floor debates on the P7.2-trillion national budget for next year, with its finance committee’s submission to the plenary of the chamber’s version of the…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito said the Senate GAB has reverted “back to the basics” of funding food, health, education, employment and security.
Senate PRIB / Released

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate now girds for marathon floor debates on the P7.2-trillion national budget for next year, with its finance committee’s submission to the plenary of the chamber’s version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB).
“Before we focus on complicated matters, we should focus what limited resources we have on ensuring that the basic needs of our people are provided,” Ejercito said.

The Senate allocated P378.6 billion for the Department of Health and its attached agencies and corporations, including P5.4 billion for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program for the construction and improvement of government hospitals and other health facilities.

The Senate also increased to P94.2 billion the government subsidy to the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), up from the House GAB version of P74.4 billion, to help realize the zero-balance billing program and reduce patients’ out of pocket expenses.

The Senate also reduced the P48.2-billion House allocation for the DOH program Medical Assistance Program, now rebranded from the previous Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP).
The Senate only allocated P16.2 billion for MAP, a P32-billion reduction from the amount in the House GAB version.
This will reduce the patients’ dependence on guarantee letters by allocating more funds for the universal health care program.
The Senate allocated P587 billion for the Department of Public Works and Highways for its various infrastructure projects next year.
To prevent a repeat of the flood control mess, Ejercito said the agency should prioritize completion of ongoing infrastructure projects and make sure the funds are put to good use.
The Senate also restored the P33.1-billion funding cut in the House GAB version on foreign-assisted big-ticket infrastructure projects.
This will help fund key infrastructure projects, such as the Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge, Laguna Lakeshore Road Network and Pasig Marikina River Channel Improvement Project, Ejercito said.

The Senate also restored the P4.7-billion government counterpart funding for foreign assisted projects, as well as the P15-billion loan proceeds each for the continued construction of the Metro Manila Subway Project and the North-South Commuter Railway.

To address the super El Niño phenomenon, the Senate earmarked P251 billion for the Department of Agriculture to help farmers with their crops, including P4 billion for its rice program and a P1-billion augmentation for the DA contingency funds.
As a response to the West Philippine Sea issue, the Senate gave the Department of National Defense an additional P1.73 billion in funding for a total of P326.9 billion.
This would be on top of the earmarked P50 billion for the Armed Forces of the Philippines modernization, Ejercito said.
The Philippine Coast Guard in the Senate version was allocated P45.6 billion, up by P146.8 million, to support its operations and maritime security efforts.
“The presence of our Navy and Coast Guard brings confidence to our fishermen who only wish to peacefully earn an honest living in the West Philippine Sea – without threat or intimidation.”

Meanwhile, the the League of Provinces of the Philippines (LPP) has welcomed the Department of Budget and Management (DBM)’s move to allow a case-by-case review of local governments’ performance in qualifying for 2026 Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) incentives.

The agreement followed a Nov. 19 meeting between Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon and representatives of the country’s local government leagues headed by LPP national chairman Isabela Gov. Rodito Albano, who cited procurement delays, failed biddings and calamities that have slowed projects meant to deliver infrastructure and basic services to residents. — Artemio Dumlao
